- **M4** (2026-09-22T19:03:44.038Z) — Bun aborts with "error: An internal error occurred (CouldntReadCurrentDirectory)" when any ancestor directory of the cwd denies reading its ENTRIES with EPERM, which is what a macOS Seatbelt `(deny file-read-data (subpath …))` returns. Bun tolerates EACCES and fails only on EPERM, so a `chmod 111` ancestor is fine while a sandboxed one is fatal. node, npm and npx are unaffected. Repro, no bench and no model needed: `mkdir -p /tmp/t/a/b/c && chmod 111 /tmp/t/a/b`, then `bun run` from c succeeds; the same shape under a Seatbelt deny fails. The fix is to allow `file-read-data` on the ancestor directory NODES themselves — `(literal "/path/to/ancestor")`, not `(subpath …)` — after the denies, since Seatbelt applies the last matching rule: the directory can then be listed while everything inside it stays denied. Anyone sandboxing a Bun toolchain on this machine will hit this.
- **M5** (2026-09-22T19:18:08.456Z) — Claude Code transcripts write SEVERAL lines per assistant message — one per content block — and the `usage` object on them ACCUMULATES, so only the last line carries that message's true totals. Any per-turn cost or token analysis must deduplicate by message id keeping the LAST or MAX usage; keeping the first silently undercounts, badly and unevenly (over one bench cell: first 19,625 output tokens, last 73,848, and the adapter's own modelUsage 73,848). The check that catches it is to sum readable output per arm and compare with the ledger's modelUsage: a correct reader lands within a few percent, and any arm below 90% should be treated as UNMEASURED rather than reasoned about. This burned three successive analyses in bench-refresh before it was found.
- **M6** (2026-09-22T19:20:56.081Z) — Never write a fresh script for a measurement this repo already tools. handoff-bench's analysis/ has transcripts.py (Claude token classes, max per message id and requestId), orchestration_spend.py (interactive spend, same dedup) and metrics.py (per-cell metrics, cost read from the LEDGER's adapter-reported usage, never from transcripts). A parallel implementation written beside them produced three successive wrong cost tables in one night, because it repeated a trap those files had already documented and solved. The rule: use or extend the existing script; if a fresh one is genuinely needed, reconcile it against the existing one on a known case — a cell whose adapter-reported total you already have — and trust no number from it until the two agree within a few percent. "Read the relevant file first" does not scale; "do not re-derive alongside working tooling, and reconcile when you must" is checkable.

- **M8** (2026-09-28T02:39:10.202Z) — Batch-calling Claude Code on the operator's plan (a grader, a judge, any `claude -p` loop) must NOT use `--bare`: --bare skips keychain reads, so every call returns "Not logged in · Please run /login" with is_error true and exit 0 (found 2026-09-28 on 2.1.283 while building 5.3's grader). The working isolation is the bench runner's own recipe, from an EMPTY scratch cwd: `claude -p --no-session-persistence --setting-sources project,local --strict-mcp-config --mcp-config '{"mcpServers":{}}' --output-format json --json-schema <schema> --disallowedTools Bash Edit Write Read Glob Grep WebFetch WebSearch Agent NotebookEdit TodoWrite`. That loads no user hooks, no CLAUDE.md and no MCP server (so a grader can never write a sofar record), and returns `structured_output` in the JSON result. Codex's equivalent: `codex exec -m <model> -s read-only --ephemeral --skip-git-repo-check -C <scratch> --output-schema <file> -o <file>` with the prompt on stdin.
